chapter: Leading his own band in New York
title: The Queens Terrace, 1939: Jackie Gleason and steady work
summary: Two weeks at the Queens Terrace turn into two years, with RKO theatre dates and piano players Phillips and Duncan.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Where else were you working? You actually didn't have to go out of New York; did you?
No, I stayed here.
For a couple of years you didn't go out of New York at all, did you?
No, I didn't because when I left out of those places, I went to Queens Terrace.
The Queens Terrace was where? Forest Hills?
No, that's in Woodside.
How long were you there?
Two years.
Two years in a stretch?
I went in there for two weeks and stayed for two years. You know who was there? Jackie Gleason. Alan King.
That must have been a pretty popular spot.
It was the biggest thing around.
We went in there and they used to close that place in the summer, and we drew so many people in that place that we kept it open the whole summer that year.
This is around when, 1939?
Latter part of '3 and all of '39.
What kind of money were you making?
We weren't making a heck of a lot of money, but it was a steady thing and they booked us in some theatres as extra. At that time we were doing RKO Theatres.
I'm sure you had a manager by this time? You weren't getting all these jobs yourself, were you?
I was getting most of these jobs myself. I didn't get an agent until
later, and I got Billy Shaw.
Now at Queens Terrace, you had basically the band that you had for a couple of years.
I had Bob Carroll, Willard Brown.
You had different piano players?
I had Lloyd Phillips first. Hank Duncan came in later.
(Side B of Tape 3 concludes at this point.)
